questions.knowledgeNote: (x-h)²+(y-k)²=r²: expand once, then compare with x²+y²+2gx+2fy+c=0.
questions.question: Q1(a). Find the equation of the circle with centre at (4, 5) and radius 3.
questions.solution: Standard form: (x-4)²+(y-5)² = 3². Expand: x²-8x+16+y²-10y+25 = 9, so x²+y²-8x-10y+32 = 0. Boxed x²+y²-8x-10y+32 = 0 (matches the printed key, book p442).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.15 Ex 15.1 Q1(a); book p441 = PDF p468 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Centre at the origin and diameter 8 means radius 4; the general form collapses to x²+y²=r².
questions.question: Q1(b). Find the equation of the circle with centre at (0, 0) and diameter 8.
questions.solution: Radius = 8/2 = 4, centre (0,0): x²+y² = 4². Boxed x²+y² = 16 (matches the printed key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.15 Ex 15.1 Q1(b); book p441 = PDF p468 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: When r² = p²+q² the constant term cancels exactly to zero — the circle passes through the origin.
questions.question: Q1(c). Find the equation of the circle with centre at (p, q) and radius √(p²+q²).
questions.solution: (x-p)²+(y-q)² = p²+q² → x²-2px+p²+y²-2qy+q² = p²+q², so x²+y²-2px-2qy = 0. Boxed x²+y²-2px-2qy = 0 (matches the printed key); note it passes through (0,0), as the radius equals the distance of the centre from the origin.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.15 Ex 15.1 Q1(c); book p441 = PDF p468 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: "Through the origin" means r² = h²+k², so the constant term again vanishes.
questions.question: Q1(d). Find the equation of the circle with centre at (4, -1) and through the origin.
questions.solution: r² = (4-0)²+(-1-0)² = 17. (x-4)²+(y+1)² = 17 → x²+y²-8x+2y+17 = 17. Boxed x²+y²-8x+2y = 0 (matches the printed key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.15 Ex 15.1 Q1(d); book p441 = PDF p468 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Two diameters of a circle meet at its centre, so the centre is the intersection of the given lines.
questions.question: Q1(e). Find the equation of the circle whose two diameters are x + y = 6 and x + 2y = 8 and radius 10.
questions.solution: Centre = intersection of x+y = 6 and x+2y = 8: subtract → y = 2, then x = 4, so centre (4, 2). With r = 10: (x-4)²+(y-2)² = 100 → x²+y²-8x-4y+20 = 100. Boxed x²+y²-8x-4y-80 = 0. FLAG (print/key mismatch): the printed Answers, book p442, give x²+y²-16x+4y-32 = 0, i.e. centre (8,-2), radius 10. That centre lies on x+y = 6 but NOT on the printed x+2y = 8 (8-4 = 4 ≠ 8), so one printed line and the key disagree. Both forms are filed: as-printed x²+y²-8x-4y-80 = 0 (centre (4,2)) and key form x²+y²-16x+4y-32 = 0 (centre (8,-2), which would follow if the second diameter read x-2y = 12, since 8-2(-2) = 12).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.15 Ex 15.1 Q1(e); book p441 = PDF p468 (vision read); key book p442 = PDF p469 (350-dpi zoom)

questions.knowledgeNote: Centre is given; the "point of intersection" supplies the radius.
questions.question: Q1(f). Find the equation of the circle with centre at (1, 5) and through the point of intersection of the lines 2x - y = 5 and 3x + y = 10.
questions.solution: Solve 2x-y = 5, 3x+y = 10: adding gives 5x = 15, x = 3, y = 1. So P(3,1) and r² = (3-1)²+(1-5)² = 4+16 = 20. (x-1)²+(y-5)² = 20 → x²+y²-2x-10y+26 = 20. Boxed x²+y²-2x-10y+6 = 0. FLAG (print/key mismatch): the printed key, book p442, reads x²+y²+2x-10y-6 = 0, which is the circle of centre (-1, 5) through the same point P (r² = 16+16 = 32). The printed centre "(+1, 5)" appears to be a sign slip; the key form is filed alongside.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.15 Ex 15.1 Q1(f); book p441 = PDF p468 (300-dpi zoom read); key book p442 = PDF p469

questions.knowledgeNote: Diameter form: (x-x₁)(x-x₂)+(y-y₁)(y-y₂) = 0.
questions.question: Q1(g). Find the equation of the circle with (0, 0) and (4, 7) as the ends of a diameter.
questions.solution: (x-0)(x-4)+(y-0)(y-7) = 0 → x²-4x+y²-7y = 0. Boxed x²+y²-4x-7y = 0 (matches the printed key); centre (2, 7/2), r = √(4+49/4) = √65/2.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.15 Ex 15.1 Q1(g); book p441 = PDF p468 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Concentric circles share g and f; only the constant term changes.
questions.question: Q1(h). Find the equation of the circle concentric with x² + y² + 8x - 6y + 1 = 0 and radius 3.
questions.solution: g = 4, f = -3 → centre (-4, 3). With r = 3: x²+y²+8x-6y+(16+9-9) = 0 → x²+y²+8x-6y+16 = 0. Boxed x²+y²+8x-6y+16 = 0 (matches the printed key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.15 Ex 15.1 Q1(h); book p441 = PDF p468 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Same centre, radius = distance from the centre to the given point.
questions.question: Q1(i). Find the equation of the circle concentric with x² + y² - 8x + 12y + 15 = 0 and passing through (5, 4).
questions.solution: Centre (4, -6). r² = (5-4)²+(4+6)² = 1+100 = 101. x²+y²-8x+12y+(16+36-101) = 0 → x²+y²-8x+12y-49 = 0. Boxed x²+y²-8x+12y-49 = 0 (matches the printed key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.15 Ex 15.1 Q1(i); book p441 = PDF p468 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Intercepts a and b on the axes through the origin give the circle x²+y²-ax-by = 0 (Thales: the origin sees the segment AB at a right angle).
questions.question: Q1(j). Find the equation of the circle passing through the origin and making intercepts equal to 3 and 4 from the positive x and y-axes respectively.
questions.solution: Points: (0,0), (3,0), (0,4). General form with c = 0: 9+6g = 0 → g = -3/2; 16+8f = 0 → f = -2. Equation x²+y²-3x-4y = 0. Boxed x²+y²-3x-4y = 0 (matches the printed key); centre (3/2, 2), r = 5/2 (the hypotenuse of the 3-4-5 triangle is the diameter).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.15 Ex 15.1 Q1(j); book p441 = PDF p468 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Centre on a line + two points on the circle: the centre is equidistant from both points, giving a second linear equation.
questions.question: Q1(k). Find the equation of the circle whose centre lies on x + 3y + 1 = 0 and which passes through (5, 3) and (-2, 2).
questions.solution: Let the centre be (h,k) with h = -3k-1. Equidistance: (h-5)²+(k-3)² = (h+2)²+(k-2)² → -10h-6k+34 = 4h-4k+8 → 14h+2k = 26 → 7h+k = 13. Substituting h = -3k-1: -21k-7+k = 13 → k = -1, h = 2. Centre (2,-1), r² = (2-5)²+(-1-3)² = 25. x²+y²-4x+2y+(4+1-25) = 0. Boxed x²+y²-4x+2y-20 = 0 (matches the printed key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.15 Ex 15.1 Q1(k); book p441 = PDF p468 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Touching the x-axis means the radius equals |k|, the distance from the centre to y = 0.
questions.question: Q2(a). Find the equation of the circle with centre (3, 4) touching the x-axis.
questions.solution: Distance from (3,4) to the x-axis = 4, so r = 4. (x-3)²+(y-4)² = 16 → x²+y²-6x-8y+9 = 0. Boxed x²+y²-6x-8y+9 = 0 (matches the printed key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.15 Ex 15.1 Q2(a); book p441 = PDF p468 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Touching the y-axis means r = |h|; keeping r as a symbol keeps the a² term in the constant.
questions.question: Q2(b). Find the equation of the circle with centre (a, b) touching the y-axis.
questions.solution: Distance from (a,b) to the y-axis = |a|, so r = a. (x-a)²+(y-b)² = a² → x²+y²-2ax-2by+b² = 0. Boxed x²+y²-2ax-2by+b² = 0 (matches the printed key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.15 Ex 15.1 Q2(b); book p441 = PDF p468 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Distance from a point to a line: |ax₀+by₀+c|/√(a²+b²) — this is the radius when the line is a tangent.
questions.question: Q2(c). Find the equation of the circle with centre (4, 5) touching the line 3x - 4y + 18 = 0.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.15 Ex 15.1 Q2(c); book p441 = PDF p468 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Touching both axes forces |h| = |k| = r; the given line then fixes the sign and the size.
questions.question: Q2(d). Find the equation of the circle whose centre lies on 3x - 5y = 4 and which touches both the axes.
questions.solution: Touching both axes → centre (±r, ±r) with radius r. Put (h,k) = (t,t): 3t-5t = 4 → t = -2. Centre (-2,-2), r = 2: x²+y²+4x+4y+(4+4-4) = 0. Boxed x²+y²+4x+4y+4 = 0 (matches the printed key). (The other sign choices contradict 3h-5k = 4.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.15 Ex 15.1 Q2(d); book p441 = PDF p468 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Two circles satisfy "touches both axes through (2,1)": a small one in the first quadrant near the point and a large one outside it.
questions.question: Q2(e). Find the equation of the circle which touches each axis and passes through (2, 1).
questions.solution: Centre (t,t), radius |t|; through (2,1): (2-t)²+(1-t)² = t² → 5-6t+t² = 0 → t = 1 or t = 5. t = 1: x²+y²-2x-2y+1 = 0. t = 5: x²+y²-10x-10y+25 = 0. Boxed x²+y²-2x-2y+1 = 0 and x²+y²-10x-10y+25 = 0 (both match the printed key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.15 Ex 15.1 Q2(e); book p441 = PDF p468 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Tangency at (a,0) and (0,a) pins the centre to (a,a) and the radius to a.
questions.question: Q2(f). Find the equation of the circle which touches the coordinate axes at (a, 0) and (0, a).
questions.solution: The radius to (a,0) is perpendicular to the x-axis, so the centre is (a,a) and r = a: (x-a)²+(y-a)² = a² → x²+y²-2ax-2ay+a² = 0. Boxed x²+y²-2ax-2ay+a² = 0 (matches the printed key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.15 Ex 15.1 Q2(f); book p441 = PDF p468 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Centre on a given line + fixed radius + tangent to a line: solve |distance| = 4 for the free parameter.
questions.question: Q2(g). Find the equation of the circle with radius 4 and centre on 13x + 4y = 32 which touches the line 3x + 4y = 12.
questions.solution: Let the centre be (h,k) with 13h+4k = 32 → k = (32-13h)/4. Tangency: |3h+4k-12|/5 = 4 → |3h+32-13h-12| = 20 → |20-10h| = 20 → h = 0 or h = 4. h = 0 → k = 8, centre (0,8): x²+y²-16y+48 = 0. h = 4 → k = -5, centre (4,-5): x²+y²-8x+10y+25 = 0. Boxed x²+y²-16y+48 = 0, x²+y²-8x+10y+25 = 0 (both match the printed key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.15 Ex 15.1 Q2(g); book p441 = PDF p468 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Given x²+y²+2gx+2fy+c=0: centre (-g,-f), radius √(g²+f²-c).
questions.question: Q3(a). Find the centre and radius of the circle x² + y² - 12x - 4y = 9.
questions.solution: g = -6, f = -2, c = -9 → centre (6,2); r = √(36+4+9) = 7. Boxed centre (6, 2), radius 7 (matches the printed key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.15 Ex 15.1 Q3(a); book p441 = PDF p468 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Fractional coefficients are fine — read g and f straight off the halved coefficients.
questions.question: Q3(b). Find the centre and radius of the circle x² + y² - 3x + 2y - 3/4 = 0.
questions.solution: g = -3/2, f = 1, c = -3/4 → centre (3/2, -1); r = √(9/4+1+3/4) = √4 = 2. Boxed centre (3/2, -1), radius 2 (matches the printed key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.15 Ex 15.1 Q3(b); book p441 = PDF p468 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: First divide by the leading coefficient 4 so that x² and y² have coefficient 1.
questions.question: Q3(c). Find the centre and radius of the circle 4(x² + y²) + 12ax - 6ay - a² = 0.
questions.solution: Divide by 4: x²+y²+3ax-(3/2)ay-a²/4 = 0, so g = 3a/2, f = -3a/4, c = -a²/4. Centre (-3a/2, 3a/4); r = √(9a²/4+9a²/16+a²/4) = √(49a²/16) = 7a/4. Boxed centre (-3a/2, 3a/4), radius 7a/4 (matches the printed key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.15 Ex 15.1 Q3(c); book p441 = PDF p468 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Three points determine a circle; the intercept form is the fastest route when two points are on the axes.
questions.question: Q4(a). Find the equation of the circle passing through (0, 0), (a, 0) and (0, b).
questions.solution: c = 0 from (0,0); a²+2ga = 0 → g = -a/2; b²+2fb = 0 → f = -b/2. Equation x²+y²-ax-by = 0. Boxed x²+y²-ax-by = 0. FLAG: the printed key, book p442, reads x²+y²-ax-bx = 0 — the second variable is a print slip (the point is (0,b), so the term must be -by; AB is a diameter, centre (a/2, b/2)).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.15 Ex 15.1 Q4(a); book p441 = PDF p468 (vision read); key book p442 = PDF p469 (350-dpi zoom)

questions.knowledgeNote: General form through three points: three linear equations in g, f, c.
questions.question: Q4(b). Find the equation of the circle passing through (1, 2), (3, 1) and (-3, -1).
questions.solution: x²+y²+2gx+2fy+c = 0 at the three points: 2g+4f+c = -5; 6g+2f+c = -10; -6g-2f+c = -10. The last two give c = -10 and 12g+4f = 0 → f = -3g; then 2g-12g = 5 → g = -1/2, f = 3/2. Boxed x²+y²-x+3y-10 = 0 (matches the printed key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.15 Ex 15.1 Q4(b); book p441 = PDF p468 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Circumcircle of a triangle: find the three vertices as line intersections, then solve for g, f, c.
questions.question: Q4(c). Find the equation of the circle circumscribing the triangle whose sides are x + y = 6, 2x + y = 4 and x + 2y = 5.
questions.solution: Vertices: x+y = 6 with 2x+y = 4 → (-2, 8); x+y = 6 with x+2y = 5 → (7, -1); 2x+y = 4 with x+2y = 5 → (1, 2). At the three points: -4g+16f+c = -68; 14g-2f+c = -50; 2g+4f+c = -5. Subtracting: 6g-12f = 63 and 12g-6f = -45 → g = -17/2, f = -19/2, c = 50. Boxed x²+y²-17x-19y+50 = 0 (matches the printed key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.15 Ex 15.1 Q4(c); book p441 = PDF p468 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Four points are concyclic iff one circle passes through all of them — find the circle from three, then test the fourth.
questions.question: Q5. Show that the points (3, 3), (6, 4), (7, 1) and (4, 0) are concyclic. Find the centre and radius of the circle.
questions.solution: Fit x²+y²+2gx+2fy+c = 0 through (3,3), (6,4), (7,1): 6g+6f+c = -18; 12g+8f+c = -52; 14g+2f+c = -50. Subtracting: 6g+2f = -34 → 3g+f = -17, and 2g-6f = 2 → g-3f = 1. With g = 1+3f: 3+9f+f = -17 → f = -2, g = -5, then c = -18+30+12 = 24. Circle: x²+y²-10x-4y+24 = 0, centre (5,2), r = √(25+4-24) = √5. Test the fourth point (4,0): 16+0-40-0+24 = 0 ✓, so all four are concyclic. Cross-check by perpendicular bisectors: of (3,3)-(7,1) is y = 2x-8 and of (6,4)-(4,0) is 2y = -x+9, meeting at (5,2) ✓. Boxed centre (5, 2), radius √5 (matches the printed key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.15 Ex 15.1 Q5; book p442 = PDF p469 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Intersect the chord line with the circle to get the diameter's endpoints, then use the diameter form.
questions.question: Q6. If y - x = 2 is the equation of a chord of the circle x² + y² + 2x = 0, find the equation of the circle of which this chord is a diameter.
questions.solution: Substitute y = x+2: x²+(x+2)²+2x = 0 → 2x²+6x+4 = 0 → x²+3x+2 = 0 → x = -1, -2. Endpoints (-1,1) and (-2,0). Circle on this diameter: (x+1)(x+2)+(y-1)(y-0) = 0 → x²+3x+2+y²-y = 0. Boxed x²+y²+3x-y+2 = 0 (matches the printed key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.15 Ex 15.1 Q6; book p442 = PDF p469 (vision read); key book p442 = PDF p469
